content_voiceover: This is a Glanzmann thrombasthenia case, Ms Jeng, a twenty-five-year-old woman with a lifelong history of easy bruising, prolonged epistaxis and gum bleeding, prolonged bleeding after cuts, and mild menorrhagia without anemia, a classic mild to moderate mucocutaneous bleeding pattern. Her bleeding time is markedly prolonged at over twelve minutes, and PFA-100 closure times are prolonged on both cartridges, collagen-epinephrine over three hundred seconds and collagen-ADP over two hundred seventy-four seconds. Von Willebrand factor antigen and ristocetin cofactor activity are both normal, at one hundred eight percent and sixty-four point five percent, essentially excluding von Willebrand disease as the cause. The aggregometry traces are the diagnostic key, flat, minimal responses to collagen, ADP, and arachidonic acid, meaning the platelets fail to aggregate to essentially every physiologic agonist, but the ristocetin trace on the far right shows a normal agglutination response. This dissociation, absent aggregation but preserved ristocetin agglutination, is pathognomonic for Glanzmann thrombasthenia, a defect of integrin alphaIIb-beta3, GPIIb-IIIa, because ristocetin agglutination depends on GPIb binding VWF, not on GPIIb-IIIa.
keypoints: Absent aggregation to ADP, collagen, and AA on aggregometry
Normal ristocetin-induced agglutination - the key distinguishing clue
Diagnosis: Glanzmann thrombasthenia, GPIIb/IIIa (integrin aIIbb3) defect
Normal VWF:Ag and VWF:RCo exclude von Willebrand disease
Opposite pattern from Bernard-Soulier, where ristocetin response is abnormal
keypoint_voiceover: The diagnostic pattern here is absent platelet aggregation to collagen, ADP, and arachidonic acid, but a normal ristocetin agglutination response, which is the signature of Glanzmann thrombasthenia, a defect in the GPIIb-IIIa fibrinogen receptor. Normal von Willebrand factor levels rule out von Willebrand disease. Remember the contrast with Bernard-Soulier syndrome, where it's the ristocetin response that fails instead.
